strengths: Well-motivated problem decomposition identifying input chunking (x) and organizing function (f) challenges in agent memory
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with ablation studies and hyperparameter analysis validating the Predict-Calibrate principle
Practical efficiency gains: 88% token reduction vs. Full Context while maintaining competitive or superior performance on LoCoMo
Strong performance on temporal reasoning (0.710-0.776) demonstrates the episodic memory structure's utility for chronological reasoning
Reasonable generalization to 105K-token contexts with meaningful improvements on user preference tasks
Clear presentation with helpful visual comparisons (Figure 2) illustrating segmentation approaches
weaknesses: Cognitive science grounding is superficial: Event Segmentation Theory describes human perception, but implementation uses standard dialogue topic segmentation; Free-energy Principle involves complex Bayesian inference, but actual system simply compares predictions to ground truth

Limited technical novelty: individual components (topic segmentation, narrative summarization, error-based learning) are well-established; main contribution is system integration rather than novel mechanisms

Evaluation methodology concerns: LLM-as-judge (gpt-4o-mini) lacks human validation and may favor LLM-generated outputs; LoCoMo's 10 dialogues is insufficient for strong conclusions; F1/BLEU-1 metrics are problematic for generation tasks

Inconsistent performance against Full Context baseline: with gpt-4.1-mini, NEMORI (0.794) underperforms Full Context (0.806), contradicting main claims and suggesting benefits are task/model-dependent rather than universal

Critical technical details missing: boundary detector confidence computation (Eq. 1) unclear; episode prediction format and comparison methodology (Eq. 6) conflates narrative vs. raw conversation; semantic knowledge distillation mechanism undefined; hyperparameter choices (σ_boundary=0.7, β_max=25) unjustified
Acknowledged loss of fine-grained details on single-session-assistant tasks (83.9% vs 89.3%) without analysis of mitigation strategies or when abstraction trade-off is worthwhile
Reproducibility hindered: no code release mentioned; exact prompts for key components not provided; relies on commercial API versions that may change; no human evaluation for validation

Scalability concerns unaddressed: semantic memory database growth during long-term deployment not analyzed; no discussion of memory management, pruning, or retrieval efficiency scaling; computational cost breakdown insufficient
Narrow evaluation scope: English-only conversational tasks; generalization to non-dialogue domains unexplored; no analysis of memory type (episodic vs. semantic) benefits by question category

EM-LLM differentiation unclear: related work [33] also proposes episodic memory with predictive surprise; claimed 'top-down' vs. 'bottom-up' distinction not empirically validated; advantage over this directly relevant baseline undemonstrated

strengths: Addresses a well-motivated and practically important problem of long-term conversational memory
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including ablations, hyperparameter analysis, and generalization studies
Strong empirical results on tested benchmarks with 88% token reduction while maintaining/improving performance
Clear conceptual framework (Figure 1) mapping problems to principles to computational modules
Honest ablation study (Table 3) demonstrating complementary roles of episodic and semantic memory
Practical efficiency gains: achieves better performance with substantially fewer tokens (2,745 vs 23,653)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core components are largely existing techniques (LLM-based topic segmentation, narrative summarization, error-driven learning) repackaged with new framing

Weak cognitive science grounding: connections to Event Segmentation Theory, Free-energy Principle, and Complementary Learning Systems are primarily rhetorical rather than mechanistic; the computational implementation is generic error-driven learning, not derived from formal theory

Unfair baseline comparisons: Mem0 and Zep use commercial API indirection while Nemori uses direct LLM access, creating incomparable conditions; no justification for different model/API configurations across methods
Problematic evaluation: relies solely on LLM-judge (gpt-4o-mini) without human evaluation, inter-annotator agreement, or alternative metrics; known recency bias in LLM judges
Limited dataset diversity: only 2 specialized QA benchmarks (LoCoMo with 10 dialogues, LongMemEvalS structurally similar); no evaluation on other memory-heavy domains

Circular evaluation logic: Calibration stage (Eq. 6) compares predicted narratives against raw conversations that were used to generate those narratives, conflating representation error with knowledge discovery

Underspecified methodology: critical details insufficiently specified (boundary detection factors, combining rules, component prompts); similarity threshold σs=0.0 removes filtering; inconsistent handling of episodic memories (top-2 include full text, others are summaries)
Suspicious statistical results: implausibly small confidence intervals (±0.001), identical w/o Nemori scores across different models (0.006), no significance testing between methods

Missing critical analyses: no human evaluation of memory quality, no error analysis of failure cases (e.g., performance drop on knowledge-update tasks from 78.2% to 61.5%), no investigation of design choices (why compare narratives to raw text?)

Overstated claims: frames standard engineering (combining topic segmentation + summarization + retrieval) as 'novel self-organizing architecture' and 'solving fundamental challenges'; cognitive science used to elevate incremental improvements
Weak baseline implementations: RAG-4096 scores only 0.302, LangMem only 0.513, suggesting poor baseline configuration or unfair comparison setup
Incomplete reproducibility: prompts for boundary detector, episode generator, and knowledge distiller not provided; hyperparameter choices (σ_boundary=0.7, β_max=25) lack justification beyond k

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing real LLM limitations with principled cognitive science grounding through Event Segmentation Theory, Complementary Learning Systems, and Free-energy Principle
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across two benchmarks of different scales (24K and 105K tokens) with ablation studies, hyperparameter analysis, and generalization assessment
Strong practical results: exceeds Full Context baseline on LoCoMo with 88% token reduction; exceptional temporal reasoning performance (0.710-0.776)
Clear empirical validation of core contribution: Predict-Calibrate principle (0.615) substantially outperforms naive extraction (0.518), directly validating proactive learning from prediction gaps
Elegant problem-to-principle-to-computation framework clearly presented with good visual exposition
Strong efficiency gains with 95-96% token reduction on 105K-token LongMemEvalS while maintaining competitive accuracy
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: contributions are primarily engineering-focused combining existing techniques (LLM boundary detection, narrative summarization, dense retrieval). No novel algorithms, architectures, or training objectives introduced

Critical reproducibility gap: prompt templates for boundary detection, episode generation, and knowledge distillation are not provided, making reproduction difficult despite stated hyperparameters. LLM-judge evaluation protocol unclear

Small primary benchmark (LoCoMo: only 10 dialogues) limits confidence in generalization; secondary benchmark shows task-dependent variability with concerning performance degradation on some question types (e.g., single-session-assistant drops from 98.2% to 92.9%)
LLM-judge metric is noisy and not well-validated; while F1/BLEU-1 included, inconsistencies between metrics weaken claims. Statistical significance testing absent across multiple runs

Boundary detection mechanism not validated: no evaluation of segmentation quality, false positive/negative rates, or analysis of subtle semantic shift detection; threshold σ_boundary=0.7 appears arbitrary
Missing cost analysis: method requires 5+ LLM calls per episode (boundary detection, generation, prediction, calibration, distillation) but no total inference cost comparison with baselines provided

Model-dependent performance ceiling: with gpt-4.1-mini, Nemori (0.794) fails to exceed Full Context (0.806), suggesting effectiveness may be task/model-dependent rather than universal; implications unclear

Cognitive science framing appears post-hoc: sophisticated theories (Free-energy Principle) reduce to standard operations (retrieve → predict → compare → extract), narrowing gap between theory and implementation

Missing error analysis and failure case examination: acknowledged limitation of fine-grained detail loss on LongMemEvalS not deeply analyzed; no qualitative examples or systematic characterization of when method struggles

Design choices under-explored: semantic-to-episodic retrieval ratio (m=2k) appears arbitrary; only top-2 episodic memories retain full text without ablation justification; narrative vs. concise representation not compared

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (LoCoMo, LongMemEvalS) with thorough ablations, efficiency analysis, and third-party integration experiments demonstrating generality

Strong empirical results: matches Full Context performance, exceptional temporal reasoning gains (+15.9%), 45-64% storage reduction when integrated with external systems, demonstrates scalability on 105K token contexts
Well-structured framework with clear conceptual distinction between distillation and management stages, reasonable inductive biases (three priors), and grounding in cognitive science principles
Practical and deployable: training-free approach, compatible with existing memory systems, extensive reproducibility support including prompt templates and code availability
Clear presentation of methodology with detailed implementation details and comprehensive ablation studies showing contribution of each component
weaknesses: Weak theoretical justification: core premise that prediction error signals importance is assumed but unvalidated; connection between high prediction error and agent performance needs empirical demonstration; Predictive Coding Theory motivation is loosely connected to actual implementation

Limited technical novelty: framework is primarily a pipeline of LLM prompting operations; replaces importance-score heuristics with LLM-based prompting rather than introducing fundamentally new techniques

Unfair experimental comparisons: Mem0 and Zep baselines use different commercial APIs with unknown backbone models, while NEMORI uses gpt-4o-mini/gpt-4.1-mini, confounding backbone model quality with memory system design

Heavy LLM dependence creates reliability concerns: every step requires LLM calls with prompts, making system vulnerable to prompt brittleness; risks circular reasoning (same LLM generates predictions and judges errors); absolute token costs remain substantial (322.9k) despite efficiency claims

Limited evaluation scope: only conversational memory tested; no evaluation on other agent tasks (planning, tool use, etc.); acknowledged underperformance on Open Domain (+6.8% gap) not deeply analyzed; missing comparisons with simpler prediction-based baselines
Design concerns: fixed observation window length contradicts claim of respecting latent integrity; naive management system admits to simplicity; limited analysis of prompt sensitivity and error modes

strengths: Clear problem formulation distinguishing memory distillation from management stages, providing useful conceptual clarity for agent memory systems
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across six research questions, two datasets, multiple baselines, and detailed ablation studies demonstrating experimental thoroughness
Practical framework design enabling integration with third-party systems achieving 45-64% storage reduction while maintaining performance
Grounding in cognitive theory (Predictive Coding, Complementary Learning Systems) provides principled motivation, even if execution raises concerns
Extensive implementation details, prompts, and supplementary results support reproducibility claims
weaknesses: Weak theoretical justification: The core premise that 'prediction error indicates what deserves memory' is asserted rather than rigorously derived from predictive coding theory. Why information an LLM fails to predict at t=0 should be valuable at t=future isn't established—this is a heuristic presented as principled

Limited technical novelty: Episodic integration via partitioning and narrativization is straightforward; the core contribution (LLM comparison of actual vs. predicted content) is a reasonable heuristic but not technically deep. Explicit admission that management is 'naive' undermines claims of a complete contribution

Unfair experimental comparison: NEMORI uses specific LLM models for both memory and answering; some baselines use different APIs. This conflates memory quality with backbone model effects. Additionally, Full Context achieves 80.6 vs. NEMORI's 80.8 on gpt-4.1-mini (0.2% difference)—essentially equivalent despite added complexity

Heavy reliance on LLM-as-judge with circularity: Primary metric uses gpt-4o-mini to evaluate systems built with same model family. No human evaluation, no statistical significance tests despite known LLM judge limitations. F1/BLEU appear secondary despite being more direct measures

Complexity contradicts efficiency claims: Multiple LLM calls (partitioning, narrativization, schema synthesis, distillation, consolidation) with 38.3% cost from narrativization and 30.3% from distillation. 'Training-free' is misleading—requires elaborate, tuned prompts (Appendix D). Efficiency gains attribution unclear

Unexplained model-dependent variance: Removing semantic retrieval causes -25.1% on gpt-4o-mini but -4.8% on gpt-4.1-mini (5x difference). This inconsistency and model-dependence is unaddressed and concerning

Consistent underperformance on knowledge-intensive tasks: Open Domain subset shows 3-7% underperformance. Explanation that this requires backbone model knowledge (Appendix B.2) inadvertently shows NEMORI fails when knowledge inference is needed, limiting practical applicability

Limited evaluation scope: Only dialogue-based tasks with no evidence of applicability to agentic workflows (code, tool use, planning). LoCoMo has only 10 dialogues. No comparison to simpler distillation heuristics (importance scoring, TF-IDF, confidence-based). Third-party integration tested on only 2 systems

Reproducibility gaps despite claims: Prompt optimization process undescribed. Were prompts hand-crafted or tuned on training data? Hyperparameter choices (Ke=Km=5, Ks=10, τ=0.70) appear arbitrary with no sensitivity analysis. Promise of code redacted for review

Unexplored central design decisions: No validation of consolidation logic (new/merge/conflict frequency). No ablation comparing prediction error to simpler heuristics. Figure 2 shows performance robust to window size (w=5-40 similar)—questioning necessity of LLM-based partitioning
Inconsistent representation prior validation: Claim that narrative representations aid retrieval, but Table 6 shows marginal differences (76.9 vs 77.0 for N→N vs N→P). Not empirically compelling

Statistical rigor absent: No confidence intervals, significance tests, or multiple runs reported. LLM-as-judge evaluation inherently noisy; improvements sometimes <1% (e.g., 80.8 vs 80.6) without statistical validation

strengths: Clear cognitive science motivation using predictive coding theory with well-articulated three priors (structure, representation, distillation) that guide principled system design
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with two complementary datasets, extensive ablations (RQ1-RQ6), and thorough documentation including detailed prompts and case studies
Significant practical efficiency gains: 59.5% reduction in LLM calls, 88% token reduction at inference, with 45-64% storage reduction when integrated with third-party systems
Strong empirical scalability results showing prediction error distillation becomes increasingly valuable on longer contexts (+16.7% on 105K tokens vs +1.0% on 9K tokens)
Particularly strong performance on temporal reasoning tasks (+15.9% over strongest baseline) through episode-centric design that front-loads reasoning during memory formation
Well-designed cascade of episodic narrative generation followed by prediction-error-based distillation with clean separation between distillation and management concerns
Management-agnostic architecture demonstrated through successful integration with third-party systems (A-MEM, MemoryOS) showing framework generalizability
weaknesses: Insufficient rigorous justification for prediction error as the optimal signal for memory utility; the connection between biological predictive coding and agent memory retention is intuitive but not formally established, and direct distillation (NEMORI-s) performs only 11% worse, suggesting prediction error may be one useful signal among alternatives rather than essential

Unfair experimental comparisons where some baselines (Mem0, Zep) use commercial APIs while NEMORI uses the same LLM backbone (gpt-4o-mini), undermining claims of 'strongest average performance' without adequate mitigation strategies
Consistent performance gaps on Open Domain questions (6.8% on gpt-4.1-mini, 3.8% on gpt-4o-mini) highlighting practical limitations for real-world scenarios requiring background knowledge injection

Complex cascading LLM pipeline (4+ calls per episode) with no error propagation analysis, robustness evaluation to prompt variations, or testing with weaker models despite claims of 'training-free' approach

Critical design hyperparameters (window length w, threshold τ=0.70, distillation parameters Ke/Km/Ks) lack principled justification or principled selection methods, appearing to require dataset-specific tuning
Semantic memory quality not directly validated through human evaluation; unclear what types of information are successfully extracted and why prediction error specifically targets valuable knowledge

Weak native management implementation showing minimal impact in ablations (64.6 vs 65.0) and potentially not exercising full capabilities; episodic integration uses only embedding similarity without considering temporal proximity
